column5: I have celiacs and am sensitive to cross contact. Many restaurants have food which is labeled gluten free but is not actually safe for me to eat. I have to decide how much I trust the waiter, read their body language to try to tell whether they know what they're talking about, and whether they are taking me seriously or not. At grocery stores, labeling is inconsistent and incomplete. In the US where I live, food labels include 'wheat' in allergen lists but don't include 'gluten', so products which contain rye or barley won't have any warning that they contain gluten. I've seen products labeled (and certified) as gluten free which also have the warning 'may contain wheat'. It's an FDA or USDA labeling problem IMO they need to fix this.
column6: Google it, Read the label carefully, Ask the staff or whoever made it, Use an app, Avoid anything I'm uncertain about
column7: Yes, frequently, due to cross contact. I have gone to restaurants that are largely gluten free after researching them in advance, ordered a gluten free menu item, confirmed it's gluten free with the staff, noted that it's a severe gluten allergy and sensitive to cross contact - and then still gotten sick. This is how celiacs works. A lot of celiacs just never eat at restaurants or other people's homes.
column8: Clear gluten free labeling on EVERYTHING that's gf. Clear 'contains gluten' labeling on EVERYTHING that contains gluten. Clear 'may contain gluten / made on shared equipment' labeling.
